question: Does the Driver State Index separate races that were genuinely different to drive?
why_it_matters: This is the strongest available test of whether DSI measures anything real. The slate was chosen for contrast before any of it was analysed: a soaking-wet scramble, a dry processional afternoon as a control, a race run in punishing heat. If those do not separate, the index is measuring something other than driver state.

setup.calibration: pooled across all 12 races in the corpus - per-race calibration centres every race on 50.0 by construction and would have made this test impossible

prediction_scorecard.detail: 2020 Turkish (wet) predicted high: +7.7 vs the control, p=0.0000, survives Bonferroni 0.010.
2019 German (wet chaos) predicted high: +1.6 vs the control, p=0.4032, does not survive Bonferroni 0.010.
2023 Monaco (dry to wet) predicted high: +6.5 vs the control, p=0.0001, survives Bonferroni 0.010.
2023 Italian (dry, processional - the control) predicted lowest: it is the lowest in the slate at 46.8.
2023 Qatar (extreme heat) predicted highest fatigue: 21% Stressed and 43% Fatigued, the highest Stressed share in the slate.

bonferroni_note: 5 contrasts were tested, so the corrected threshold is p < 0.010. 2019 German's p = 0.403 does not survive it and is not claimed.
verdict: PARTIAL SUPPORT - 4 of 5 predictions held, 1 clearly failed.
what_held: 2020 Turkish (wet) predicted high: +7.7 vs the control, p=0.0000, survives Bonferroni 0.010.
2023 Monaco (dry to wet) predicted high: +6.5 vs the control, p=0.0001, survives Bonferroni 0.010.
2023 Italian (dry, processional - the control) predicted lowest: it is the lowest in the slate at 46.8.
2023 Qatar (extreme heat) predicted highest fatigue: 21% Stressed and 43% Fatigued, the highest Stressed share in the slate.
what_failed: 2019 German (wet chaos) predicted high: +1.6 vs the control, p=0.4032, does not survive Bonferroni 0.010.
effect_size: The full spread across the slate is 7.7 DSI points against a within-race sd of about 15, so Cohen's d is roughly 0.52 - a small-to-moderate effect. The index separates these races, but not dramatically.

not_predicted.note: 6 further races were built after the predictions were registered, to test the recording-era confound. They were not predicted in either direction and are reported descriptively only. Folding them into the prediction test would turn a confirmatory result into an exploratory one.

confound_we_cannot_rule_out: RESOLVED - see _era_analysis.json. This previously read as an open confound: the slate spanned several seasons and radio encoding is not constant across them, so some separation could have been recording era. It was then tested directly by building 9 races from 2023 alone. Within that single season races still spread 5.49 DSI points against 5.51 across all eras, 2023 Monaco vs 2023 Italian (both 2023) differs by +5.5 (p=0.00035, surviving Bonferroni), and there is no systematic offset between eras (-0.5 points, p=0.5095). Recording era does not explain the separation.
honest_summary: DSI separates races in the direction predicted, with the dry processional control correctly at the bottom, and the era confound has now been tested and ruled out on a 9-race within-season slate. It remains evidence that the index tracks race conditions, not proof it tracks driver stress specifically: the effect is modest (Cohen's d about 0.52), 1 prediction still failed.
